info.title: Club Planner Partner API
info.description: # Welcome The **Club Planner Partner API** lets approved partners read and write data on a Club Planner platform in a stable, versioned way. Use it to integrate booking, check-in, payments, member data and more with your own systems. ## Authentication Every request must carry your partner API key in the **`X-API-Key`** header (or, alternatively, the standard `Authorization: Bearer ` header — both are equivalent). Keys are issued and revoked by the platform administrator in *Settings → Platform → Partner API*. A **401** response means the key is missing, invalid, expired or has been deactivated. ## Multi-club platforms A Club Planner platform database can host one or more clubs. Endpoints that target a specific club take a **`clubId`** — call `GET /api/partner/v1/club` first to discover the available ids and pick the right one for each call. ## Club-limited keys A key can be limited to one club of the platform (or left open for all clubs). With a club-limited key: - A `clubId` (or `owner`) of another club returns **403**, in the query, in the path and in a request body. - Omitting `clubId`, or passing `0` / `-1` (all clubs / the current club), means the key's own club. - Creating a record without a `clubId` creates it in the key's club. - Lists only contain records of the key's club, plus records shared by all clubs (`clubId`/`ownerId` 0). `GET /api/partner/v1/club` only returns the key's club. - Reading a single record that belongs to another club returns **403**. ## Per-namespace access Each key is granted **None / Read / Read + write** access independently for each namespace: `General`, `Employee`, `Members`, `Planner`, `Leads`, `Financial`, `CheckIn`. A `GET` or `HEAD` needs *read*; any other method needs *read + write*. A **403** response means your key does not have sufficient access for that namespace. ## Rate limiting A key may have a per-period call limit (e.g. *N* requests per 5 minutes, hour, day or month). Each request counts once. When the limit is reached the API returns **429 Too Many Requests** until the next period resets. ## Versioning All endpoints are prefixed with **`/api/partner/v1/`**. Breaking changes go in a new major version (`/v2/`); the previous version stays available alongside. ## Errors | Status | Meaning | |---|---| | 400 | Bad request (validation, malformed body) | | 401 | Missing / invalid / expired API key | | 403 | Key lacks access to the namespace, or is limited to a different club | | 404 | Resource does not exist or is out of scope for your key | | 429 | Rate limit reached for this key | | 5xx | Server error — please retry | ## Logging When logging is enabled on your key, each call is recorded (method, path, status, duration). Platform admins can review this for support and audit purposes. ## Use with AI assistants (MCP) If you want to call this API from **Claude Desktop, Cursor, Zed** or any other [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io)-aware tool, install the official MCP server — it adds your `X-API-Key` automatically and exposes this OpenAPI spec as a resource so the assistant discovers every endpoint on its own. No per-endpoint wiring needed. Add this to your MCP client config (Claude Desktop example): ```json { "mcpServers": { "clubplanner": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@clubplanner/partner-api-mcp"], "env": { "CLUBPLANNER_URL": "https://your-club.clubplanner.app", "CLUBPLANNER_API_KEY": "cp_..." } } } } ``` Source and details on npm: [@clubplanner/partner-api-mcp](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@clubplanner/partner-api-mcp). ## Getting started 1. Ask the platform administrator for a partner API key. 2. Send `X-API-Key: ` on every request. 3. Call `GET /api/partner/v1/ping` to verify connectivity. 4. Call `GET /api/partner/v1/club` to discover the `clubId` you want to work with. 5. Explore the endpoints in the sidebar — each one shows request/response shapes and a code sample.

get.description: Unauthenticated health check. Returns the service status and the current UTC time.

Returns the current on/off state of each gate (8 or 32, depending on the club_group_policy parameter) for a Loxone Ethernet relay to act on.
